correctness.rationale: All common subsequences of the opposing one-switch words are monochromatic, so an SCS alignment shares s=max(min(a,d),min(b,c)) positions of one letter. The union-of-embeddings argument forces four explicit unique-output shuffle forms, disjoint across the two shared-letter classes by output letter counts. Their binomial sizes sum to the formula with correct tie indicators. Strict central-binomial comparison covers r0!=r1 and ties>=2; the exhaustive s=1 boundary pair partition yields exactly the balanced a=c=1 or b=d=1 maximizers. The mathematical proof handles every positive quadruple and edge equality. Checkers independently enumerate 655464 candidate words across 715 tuples and recursively calculate all 1296 tuples with entries at most six; finite checks do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The exact number of distinct shortest-supersequence outputs is a natural reconstruction ambiguity invariant, often much smaller than the number of merge paths. Resolving all four independent block sizes by two disjoint constructive binomial branches, including tied LCS modes, is an all-length classification. Characterizing precisely the inputs that saturate the known global upper bound is additional meaningful equality structure not implied by the bound. No small finite experiment is used as the sole mathematical contribution.
